title: Telemetry-driven rollback safety net for staggered model introductions
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Implement a telemetry-driven safety net that automates safe pauses and rollbacks during staggered/staged model introductions (canary, A/B, and shadow). The goal is to give product and SRE teams a declarative policy that evaluates multiple signal domains (latency, 5xx/error-rate, token-level quality regression, hallucination signals from eval hooks, business metric deltas) and executes safe actions: hold, reduce traffic, rollback, or escalate for manual review. This ticket covers the policy definition, the runtime enforcement hooks, a simulation mode for dry-run evaluation, and integration points with Console alarms and Rollout UI.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL exists for: step schedule, cohort selectors, weighted traffic, escalation windows, and multi-signal thresholding
Runtime evaluates telemetry windows and triggers one of: hold, decelerate (reduce weight by X%), rollback to previous pinned model, or escalate to on-call with a reproducible trace
Simulation mode emits expected actions without modifying traffic and produces annotated diffs in the Console
Telemetry schema added to platform events and covered in the telemetry contract doc
End-to-end test covers staged canary with induced latency and model-score regression that results in automatic rollback
Docs added to Rollouts section in Console (how to author policies and interpret safety actions)
comments: 2026-02-21: Triage meeting notes — prioritize multi-signal thresholds and simulation mode. PM requested ability to pin canary cohorts by customer tier.
2026-02-26: Spike completed — parsed 30s and 5m sliding windows from ingest pipeline for latency and error-rate. Found that 99th p99 must be smoothed to avoid noisy rollback triggers.
2026-03-03: Design review — agreed to include a short-circuit 'grace window' to avoid tearing down canaries for transient spikes; SRE asked for a playbook for manual overrides.
2026-03-08: Prototype PR opened for the policy DSL parser. Jonah Park suggested schema-level validation and backwards compatibility rules.
2026-03-12: QA smoke tests for simulation mode passed on staging; observed false positive rate reduced after smoothing. Next: add model-quality eval hooks and A/B stat tests.
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and validation
Integration test: simulate 10-min canary with ramp steps [1%, 5%, 20%, 50%] and induce 2x p95 latency at step 2 => expect 'hold' then 'rollback' when sustained beyond grace window
E2E: use synthetic user traffic with shadow probing enabled to validate shadow-only scoring path and ensure no impact to production until policy action
Chaos test: random transient infra failures to validate grace-window prevents unnecessary rollback
Performance test: ensure runtime decision loop adds <20ms per request on the critical path (decision done async to avoid tail latency)
A/B statistics test: ensure lift/regression detection respects multiple hypothesis corrections for simultaneous cohorts
telemetry_contract: Added fields: rollout_id, cohort_id, policy_id, decision_reason, sample_rate, model_hash
Signal windows required: latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}, request_error_rate, model_eval_score.mean, hallucination_rate_estimate
Retention: 90 days for policy debugging, 1 year aggregated for postmortems
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable simulation mode for 2 weeks for existing canaries and collect simulated actions (no traffic change)
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in small internal services (10% of traffic) with policy enforcement and 24/7 on-call coverage
Phase 3 (GA): enable as default for new canaries with UI-exposed policy templates and one-click rollback audit

Rollback behavior: immediate rollback to last pinned model when 'critical' thresholds hit or after N consecutive evaluation windows; otherwise reduce weight and wait for recovery within graceful_backoff_seconds
Escalation: include synthetic replay trace and top-5 contributing metrics in alert payload
risks: Overly-sensitive thresholds can cause unnecessary rollbacks; mitigated by grace window, hysteresis, and simulation tuning
Telemetry lag could make decisions stale; design adds sliding windows and requires min_samples threshold
Complex multi-signal policies may be hard for PMs to author; provide templates and opinionated defaults
Cross-region variance could cause localized rollbacks—policy must support region-scoped decisions
Automated rollback for private deployments must respect customer override settings and KMS-based audit logs
notes: Design decision: use a policy DSL (YAML/JSON) that compiles down to an evaluation graph executed by the runtime. This lets Console show a visualization of thresholds and expected traffic curves.

Trade-off: evaluation in fast path vs async decisioning. We implement a hybrid: lightweight gating in-line (simple weight clamps) and heavier actions via the control plane to avoid tail latency impacts.
Follow-ups: UX task for Rollouts UI to surface simulation diffs (PM backlog), SRE runbook for incident response when rollback automation misfires
Related work: dovetails with model-quality-monitoring (MQM) and the canary policy repository; coordinate with Release Engineering for dedicated pool safeguards
